title: Routing: integrate capacity signals (GPU pool saturation, queue depth) into breaker open/close decisions
creator: Mina Haddad
description:
Goal
Integrate real-time capacity signals (GPU pool saturation + queue depth / wait) into the routing service circuit breaker evaluator so that breaker open/close decisions reflect actual data-plane pressure, not just downstream error rate.

Why
We’ve historically relied on a mix of 5xx rates + latency to infer overload. During traffic spikes this leads to delayed reaction (tail latency collapses before we shed) and, worse, ambiguous 5xx/timeouts that cause client retry storms. This ticket connects “what’s happening in GPU pools right now” to the breaker state machine (ENG-4824 / ADR-0148) so we can shed earlier and more deterministically.

Non-goals
- This does not define customer-facing error taxonomy / mapping (see ENG-4823 / ADR-0147).
- This does not change runtime scheduling; we only consume the signals runtime exports.

Proposed capacity signals (initial set)
All signals must be available at routing at per-(region, pool, model_class[, tier]) granularity without exploding label cardinality.

1) GPU pool saturation
- utilization_ewma (0..1) per pool
- active_requests / max_concurrency (or equivalent “slots used”)
- prefill_tokens_per_s and decode_tokens_per_s (optional; used as secondary health indicator)

2) Queue pressure
- queue_depth (pending requests) at runtime ingress and/or scheduler
- queue_wait_p95_ms (preferred over raw depth when available)

3) Shed pressure (feedback)
- runtime_shed_rate (requests shed inside runtime due to bounded queues / memory pressure)
- shed_reason breakdown (coarse only; do not plumb high-cardinality reasons into breaker state labels)

Signal transport + freshness
- Add CapacitySignalFeed RPC (routing <- runtime telemetry aggregator) with TTL semantics.
- Freshness requirement: routing should treat signals older than 3x publish interval as stale and ignore them for opening decisions (fallback to error-rate/latency only).
- Publish interval target: 1s (can be 2s if needed for overhead); routing consumes EWMA windows 5s/30s.

Breaker integration (how signals influence state)
This ticket focuses on two things:
1) “Open faster” on clear saturation/queue conditions.
2) “Close safely” only when pressure has genuinely subsided (hysteresis + cooldown already covered in ADR-0148; we’ll implement the inputs + gating here).

Open conditions (additive to existing error/latency conditions)
For each breaker key: (region, model, tier) mapped to one or more GPU pools.
- OPEN if (saturation_ewma_5s > threshold_sat_open) AND (queue_wait_p95_ms > threshold_wait_open OR queue_depth > threshold_depth_open) for >= 2 consecutive eval ticks.
- OPEN if runtime_shed_rate_5s > threshold_shed_open (used as “smoking gun” that data plane is shedding).
- OPEN if “stale signals” is false and “pool health state” is RED (aggregated signal from infra; optional if available).

Close conditions (gated)
- Only allow transition to HALF_OPEN if:
  - saturation_ewma_30s < threshold_sat_close AND queue_wait_p95_30s < threshold_wait_close
  - runtime_shed_rate_30s < threshold_shed_close
  - AND signals are fresh
- If signals are stale, close logic should fall back to current state machine rules but with extended cooldown (config default).

Key design choices / tradeoffs
- Prefer queue_wait_p95_ms over queue_depth: depth isn’t comparable across runtime versions / pool configs.
- Use multi-window EWMAs (5s for open, 30s for close) to reduce flapping while still reacting quickly.
- Staleness handling: stale capacity signals should NOT open breakers (avoid false positives if telemetry pipeline is degraded), but can block close if the breaker is currently open (safer default) unless oncall overrides.

Implementation plan
1) Routing: capacity-signal ingest + caching
- Add in-memory cache keyed by pool_id with last_updated timestamp.
- Add aggregation layer mapping breaker key (model, region, tier) -> list of pools -> aggregated saturation/queue metrics.
- Add “signal freshness” bit per breaker key.

2) Breaker evaluator: incorporate capacity signals
- Extend breaker input structure to include capacity_pressure_score + raw metrics used for debug.
- Apply thresholds from config (region/model_class defaults + overrides) supplied by ENG-4828.

3) Telemetry
- Emit routing metrics:
  - breaker_capacity_signal_stale{region, model, tier}
  - breaker_capacity_pressure_score{region, model, tier}
  - breaker_open_reason=capacity|errors|latency|manual
- Add trace annotation when breaker open decision is driven by capacity (so we can correlate with runtime graphs quickly).

4) Feature flag + rollout
- Feature flag: breaker_capacity_signals_enabled (per region + model_class).
- Canary in us-east on 1-2 hosted models; compare:
  - time-to-open during spike
  - shed rate distribution (edge vs runtime)
  - p99 latency of admitted requests
  - client-visible 429/503 mix (via ENG-4823)

Acceptance criteria
- During synthetic overload (perf-canary step load), routing opens breakers within 2–5s of sustained saturation + queue pressure.
- Breakers do not flap more than 1 transition per 10 minutes under steady-state “near threshold” load (measured in staging + canary).
- If telemetry pipeline is disrupted (signals stale), routing does not erroneously open breakers; instead it relies on error/latency signals.
- New routing metrics/traces are available and used by overload dashboard (ENG-4830) without unbounded label growth.

Open questions
- Pool mapping: for model routing that can choose among pools, do we aggregate “worst pool” vs “weighted by traffic share”? Current proposal: worst-pool for OPEN, weighted for CLOSE.
- Dedicated alignment: dedicated pools may want higher thresholds / different close gating; we’ll keep config defaults separate by tier and validate with ENG-4837.

Risks
- Stale signal false negatives could delay opening (mitigated by retaining error/latency path).
- Incorrect pool mapping could open breakers unnecessarily (mitigated by logging debug fields + shadow mode in canary).

Notes for oncall
- This work is expected to reduce ‘mystery 503’ incidents by opening earlier and shedding deterministically, but it will increase the number of explicit overload responses during spikes (expected/desired). Ensure status-page guidance is aligned before broad rollout.
comments: 2025-11-13 — Ravi Menon: Drafted initial signal list (sat + queue_wait + runtime_shed_rate). Biggest unknown is pool mapping for multi-pool routes; leaning worst-pool for OPEN to protect tail latency. Will sync with Noah/Sofia on which queue_wait stat we can trust from runtime.

2025-11-18 — Elena Popov: +1 on multi-window approach (fast open, slow close). Please ensure the ingest path has a clear ‘stale’ boolean and does not open breakers on missing telemetry. We’ve seen telemetry gaps during regional brownouts.

2025-12-02 — Allison Grant: Observability review: avoid labeling with raw pool_id in high-volume metrics; ok to include pool_id in debug logs / sampled traces only. For metrics, stick to region + model_class + tier, and maybe ‘pool_group’ if bounded.

2025-12-08 — Mina Haddad: PM/SRE concern: we need deterministic close behavior; do not close based solely on brief drops in utilization. Please implement 30s close window + cooldown gate from ADR-0148 and add a unit test for flapping near thresholds.

2026-01-04 — Ravi Menon: Implementation complete behind feature flag. Added cache TTL handling and a shadow-mode log line to compare capacity-driven decisions vs error-driven decisions. Awaiting review from Christine + Peter. Linked PR: redwood/pr-18461.

2026-01-15 — Christine Wong: Review notes: thresholds should be read from config with sane defaults even if ENG-4828 isn’t merged yet; don’t block. Also, please add metric for ‘signals stale while breaker open’ since that’s an oncall footgun. Otherwise looks good for us-east canary.
